summary: A correctness release: the thread gateway closes with byte-exact joins, 128-bit and unsigned integer semantics land, aggregates escaping confined blocks stay valid, and a broad resolution sweep removes name, constant and import hazards.

highlights.title: Spawned threads return their exact results
highlights.text: Joining a spawned worker returns its value exactly: pointer-holding struct fields keep byte-pointer arithmetic through locals and method receivers, so the result read is correct, and confined allocation rounds become ordinary main-memory pointers instead of spinning.

highlights.title: Wide integers and unsigned ordering
highlights.text: Native 128-bit values now live correctly inside vectors and structs, and unsigned 64-bit values compare, widen, divide and take remainders with full-width semantics: values with the top bit set order, widen and divide exactly instead of behaving signed.

highlights.title: Aggregates escaping confined blocks
highlights.text: A struct or vector returned from a confined block is copied to ordinary memory before the guard arena resets: inline vector fields stay valid, a push-tail arm no longer mis-arms the return path, and callers read live data instead of released arena bytes.

highlights.title: Names, constants and imports resolve exactly
highlights.text: A broad resolution sweep: enum variants no longer collide with geometry names, soft-keyword field names parse, constants re-export through public use, shadowing constants no longer hang the build, pointer spellings resolve at call sites, and checks stay enforced on optimized builds.

highlights.title: Byte and string paths go linear across the tree
highlights.text: The strnlen and concatenate-per-item sweep converts the string, escaping, encoding, hashing, parser and file-IO families to cached single-pass reads and buffer builders. Hot loops use bounds-guaranteed slices, large payloads scale linearly, and every wave is locked by a probe.

highlights.title: Thread spawn results are byte-exact
highlights.text: The spawn result buffer is main-heap and the runtime trampoline stores the full 64-bit result and done flag, so join readbacks return the exact worker value on every ABI. Acceptance: single and two-thread spawns print the exact results across repeated runs.

known_issues: Comparing containers with equality operators is pointer identity: two equal vectors compare unequal, and equal results containing vectors compare unequal; deep container equality is queued.
